info.description:
Local bookkeeping API. Conventions an agent needs before writing:

- **Unknown fields are rejected** (422 naming the field); nothing is silently dropped.
- **Posted documents are voided, not deleted**: `POST /api/<resource>/{id}/void` (invoices, bills, payments, bill payments, credit memos, expenses, journal entries, in-kind gifts, job costs). `DELETE` on one answers 405 and names the void route. A pledge that will not be paid is written off (`POST /api/invoices/{id}/write-off`), not voided.
- **`tax_rate` on a document is a fraction** (0.089 = 8.9%), kept to six places (0.08875 = 8.875%); `default_tax_rate` in settings is a percent string ("8.9"). Divide by 100.
- **`terms` names an entry on `/api/payment-terms`** (its rule gives the due date and any early-payment discount; the document keeps the term it was saved under); text that is neither on the list nor `Net N` is due in 30 days and the document's `terms_note` says so. A payment's `allocations[].discount` must be one the document's terms offer, else an administrator sends `allow_discount_override`, which the payment records.
- Enumerated fields are enums in this spec; read the allowed values here rather than guessing.

get.description:
Tell the SPA whether first-run setup is needed and whether the
current session is authenticated. When the session's company cannot be
opened now (#358: its file missing, locked or from another version),
the answer says so and still lists the companies this server serves,
so the sign-in screen keeps its choice.

Whose password the window may set (W-125): the administrators' names,
for the reset form's choice. The launcher asks with its window secret, as
it sends the reset itself; a browser, a token and a server install are
refused, so the names are not read from the sign-in page's address.

post.description:
Set a new administrator password when it is forgotten (#719): from
the desktop app's own window alone (the launcher sends this with its
window secret; a browser, an API token, Server Edition and a windowless
run are refused), with the recovery key when the file is encrypted
under one, else proven by being at the computer that holds the file.
The administrator's other sessions end, the reset is in the audit log
by how it was made, and the page signs in with the new password.

The signed-in person sets their own password (#345): an invited
accountant replacing the one-time password at the first sign-in, or
anyone changing theirs, with the current one to prove it.

First-run setup: store company/operator info and the operator password
in one transaction, then issue a session. Returns 409 if a password is
already set.

Verify the operator password and issue a session.

Rate-limited to 5/minute per IP to kill fast brute-force. argon2id's
~100ms-per-verify cost is the second line. Every attempt — success or
failure — is recorded in `login_attempts` so a slow patient attacker
pacing requests under the rate limit still shows up in the audit log.

Clear the session cookie. On a server serving several companies the
sign-in screen stays in the company signed out of (#358). Sign out bumps
the user's session version too, so a copy of the cookie taken before it
does not keep working; a sign-out still succeeds when the books cannot
be reached, or the session names no user row (a desktop or legacy
session).

Work in another company this server serves (#358).

Signed in, and the sign-in's password opened that company too: the
session moves there, signed in as the same username with the role that
company gives it, and the company's own log records the sign-in.
Otherwise the session is signed out and the sign-in screen asks for
that company's password, the username filled in.

put.description:
Edit an invoice: what the request sends changes, what it leaves out
stays as stored.

The addresses (2.31.1): a bill or ship address part sent, or
``ship_to_country``, is what the invoice gets, "" or null blanking it.
The Bill To's name and country stay the ones the invoice was billed
with. An edit that moves the invoice to another customer takes the
new customer's addresses as create does, the payer's whole Bill To
(street, name and country) and the customer's own Ship To with its
country, and a part sent with the move wins over the one copied, ""
or null blanking it. The invoice form sends no address part: its save
keeps the stored addresses, and a change of customer there takes the
new customer's. A move is refused (409 ``money_applied``) while a
payment or credit memo is applied to the invoice, naming each; an
unpaid invoice moves.

Email invoice as PDF attachment — Feature 8

Void — creates a reversing journal entry. A pay application's invoice
is voided with the application.
Mark the invoice as sent.
Apply late fees to overdue invoices past the grace period.

Forgive an open balance (a pledge that will never be paid, a small
balance not worth collecting): a credit memo flagged as a write-off,
posting DR Bad Debt Expense / CR A/R and applied to the invoice at
once. Any company, since 2.22.2 (#255); undo it by voiding the memo.

post.description:
Write off the listed invoices' balances, one credit memo each to Bad
Debt Expense, all posted together or none (#255). An invoice whose
balance is no longer under the figure (a payment landed since it was
listed), is paid, or is void is skipped and named, not written off.
Returns `{written_off: [...], skipped: [{invoice_id, reason}]}`.

Duplicate — the same sale under a new number, dated today and not
sent yet. The copy carries what the original says about the sale: its
currency and the rate it was booked at, the job, class and PO number,
and each line's item, job, class and cost code. Each line's tax is the
customer's as they stand today, and the copy is billed as of today
too: the Bill To is the payer's now and the ship-to the customer's now
(2.31.1 gate, W-73). It posts the way a new invoice does.

The copy used to drop the currency and rate, so a EUR 850.00 invoice's
duplicate was a $850.00 invoice (and posted $850 where the original
booked $935), and it dropped the job and every line's job, class and
cost code, so the copy was missing from job costing (found integrating
the 2.17.3 exploratory fixes).

schema.title: Response List Payments Api Payments Get

post.description:
Apply the unapplied part of an earlier payment — an overpayment, a
prepayment, or a payment recorded without choosing invoices — to the
same customer's open invoices.

Before this there was no way to: the credit sat on account 1100 while
every invoice still read unpaid (explore 2.17.3, macbase1 F12). Moving
money between the payment and an invoice changes which document it
settles, not the ledger: the payment already credited A/R in full. A
foreign-currency remainder relieved A/R at the payment's rate; settling
an invoice booked at another rate posts the difference as realized FX,
exactly as applying it on the day would have.

Take an early-payment discount with a payment already recorded
(#665): the customer paid 98 of 100 within the window and the 2 was not
taken then. The discount is checked against the invoice's terms on the
payment's date and its balance before the payment, posts as one taken
with the payment would (a credit memo tied to it, voided with it), and
is dated as the payment is.

Claimed before anything is read (#665: four at once each posted a
memo): an Idempotency-Key is reserved, then the payment's row is
written, so a second request waits for the first to commit and then
reads its discount and is refused; a retry with the same key answers
with the first response.

Void a payment — reverses journal entry and restores invoice balances.

An online payment posted to a provider's clearing account is reversed
against that account, never the bank, so a refund or dispute comes out of
what the provider holds (#584). The processing fee the provider kept
stays booked as an expense unless `fee_refunded` says the provider gave it
back. A payment already paid out can't be told apart per payment yet, so
the void goes through and the response carries a warning.

A deposit a payment application applied is voided with that application.

Change a received payment (#689): void it (its discounts with it, its
invoices given back their balances) and post `data` in its place, the
two linked, under the void's refusals: a closed period, money already
deposited, a deposit a payment application applied.

post.description:
Post this statement line as a register entry and link it. With
`splits` (a provider payout, #584) the other side is several accounts
instead of one category, validated like a register split.

Record an unmatched deposit as a provider payout (#584). The server
builds the split from the gross — CR the provider's clearing account for
the gross, DR the fee account for gross − net, DR the bank for the net —
so the account ids stay off the client; then it adds it the normal way,

same journal entry, so its attachments, statement matches and audit
trail stay with it. An entry a completed reconciliation holds keeps its
amount and date (a change is refused with 400, as its void is); a memo,
reference, class or job fix goes through; a change that moves an amount
to a different account in that period is refused with 409 and the
statement date until `confirm_reconciled`, then audited as such.

Deposits made, newest first — with the payments each took, and
whether it can still be voided (not void already, not reconciled).

One deposit and the payments it took. The bank register links a
deposit here (#/deposits/{id}); the link said "Page not found".

bank-entry edit rewrites a register entry: the same journal entry, its

reposted through `replace_journal_lines` — not mutated by hand — so the
deposit's statement match and audit trail stay with it; the payments it
no longer takes go back on the Make Deposits list and the new ones are
stamped with it. A deposit on a reconciled bank statement keeps its
amount and date (a change is refused with 400, as its void is).

every other document.
The slip as a page for the browser's print dialog.

Take a deposit back: post its mirror image and put every payment it

Change a recorded expense (#689): void it and post `data` in its

The checks Pay Bills wrote on a bank account that are waiting to be

A term is never deleted, so the documents saved under it keep their

Job Cost Entry each). Returns per-entry results; nothing is rolled

Post one approved time entry to its job as labor cost at the
employee's loaded rate, with burden as its own line.
Run the overtime engine over raw daily hours (FLSA + state overrides).

yet (pay_run_id IS NULL) and were entered here — same filter the

api_key.title: Api Key
api_key.description: Omit to keep the stored key. A non-empty value replaces it (stored encrypted, never returned). An empty string removes it.

AIModelsRequest.title: AIModelsRequest
AIModelsRequest.description:
What the Settings page has in its boxes right now, saved or not: the
provider picked, a key typed and not yet saved, the provider's extras.
Each overrides the saved value; nothing here is stored.

AssetAcquisition.title: AssetAcquisition
AssetAcquisition.description:
How the purchase reaches the books (services/fixed_assets.py):
paid_from a bank or card `account_id` (with a check or `reference`);
opening_balance for an asset owned before the books began (`as_of` the
day they began, `accumulated_depreciation` taken by then); a `bill_id`
or `expense_id` already entered; or in_books (nothing posts).

BankEntryDetail.title: BankEntryDetail
BankEntryDetail.description:
A register entry in the + Entry form's shape (#388): the signed
amount, the category (or the split lines), payee, memo, reference,
class and job; `reconciled_on` is the statement date of the completed
reconciliation that holds it, if one does, and `reconciled_note` the
sentence the form shows for it; `class_name` names the class (an
archived one too, which the class list leaves out). After an edit,
`uncleared` names the lines whose amount changed and so lost their
cleared mark, and `note` says so in a sentence.

BankEntryUpdate.title: BankEntryUpdate
BankEntryUpdate.description:
The + Entry form's fields again, for editing a register entry in
place (#388). A field left out keeps what the entry has (its job, its
class, its lines' own classes); `account_id` may be left out (the
entry's own) but may not name another account. On an entry a
completed reconciliation holds, the amount and date stay as they are
(400 otherwise), and a change of category or split lines is refused
with 409 until `confirm_reconciled` is true.

BankSplit.title: BankSplit
BankSplit.description:
One line of a split register entry (#330): the account it posts to
and its share of the amount, signed (money out negative, money in
positive), and its own memo. A line may carry the opposite sign from
the entry (#387): a card processor's fee on a deposit, a refund netted
against a check. Never zero. A line may name its own class and job
(an imported check's lines can); left out, it takes the entry's.

BankTransactionCreate.title: BankTransactionCreate
BankTransactionCreate.description:
A register entry: posts a journal entry. amount > 0 debits the bank
or card account (money in / card payment), amount < 0 credits it
(money out / card charge). `account_id` is the ledger account;
`bank_account_id` (the feed) is accepted for older callers. With
`splits`, the other side is several accounts whose amounts add up to
`amount` (a check that pays several things; a loan payment that is
principal and interest; a processor's deposit as the gross income and
the fee taken out, the bank taking the net); `category_account_id` is
then the first split's account, kept for older callers.

BankTransactionResponse.title: BankTransactionResponse
BankTransactionResponse.description: A statement line in the review queue.

tax_rate.title: Tax Rate
tax_rate.description: Tax rate as a FRACTION of the taxable subtotal: 0.089 means 8.9%. Not a percent — Settings.default_tax_rate is the percent form ('8.9'); divide it by 100 before sending. Values above 1 are rejected. Kept to six places, a percent to four (0.08875 means 8.875%); a finer rate is rounded half up.

BillLineCreate.title: BillLineCreate
BillLineCreate.description:
One line of a bill: a quantity and a rate, or an amount alone (#391).

A utility bill or a pest-control bill has an amount and no quantity or
rate, so a line may send ``amount`` by itself. The row is stored as
quantity 1 x rate = amount, which is what the bill says and what every
reader of the line (the journal, job costing, the PDF, the exports)
already works from; nothing downstream learns a new shape. A line that
sends a quantity or a rate is priced from them as before, and an amount
sent with them must agree to the cent or the line is refused: a client
that sends both and means the amount would otherwise be told nothing.

BillPaymentDiscountAdd.title: BillPaymentDiscountAdd
BillPaymentDiscountAdd.description:
An early-payment discount taken after the payment that paid the rest
of the bill (#665), recorded against that payment.

BillPaymentDiscountResponse.title: BillPaymentDiscountResponse
BillPaymentDiscountResponse.description:
A discount we took with this payment: the vendor credit applied to
the bill (#664).

anyOf.description: Tax rate as a FRACTION of the taxable subtotal: 0.089 means 8.9%. Not a percent — Settings.default_tax_rate is the percent form ('8.9'); divide it by 100 before sending. Values above 1 are rejected. Kept to six places, a percent to four (0.08875 means 8.875%); a finer rate is rounded half up.

BillUpdate.title: BillUpdate
BillUpdate.description:
An edit of a posted bill (#225): whatever is sent changes, the rest
stays. Lines, when sent, replace the bill's lines.

ChangeOrderUpdate.title: ChangeOrderUpdate
ChangeOrderUpdate.description: Edit a draft/pending change order. A field left out is unchanged.

ContractSummary.title: ContractSummary
ContractSummary.description:
The contract roll-up for one job — figures the Contract tab's tiles
read. Additive; a job with no contract type still answers (the money
fields fall back to the plain contract_amount).

ContractTerms.title: ContractTerms
ContractTerms.description:
The PUT body for a job's contract terms. Every field is optional —
a field left out is unchanged; a field sent as null clears it.

CostToCompleteEntry.title: CostToCompleteEntry
CostToCompleteEntry.description:
One forecast cell: a section (cost_code_id; None with cost_type "" is the
Unassigned cell), a cost type, and the amount — None clears the entry.

anyOf.description: Tax rate as a FRACTION of the taxable subtotal: 0.089 means 8.9%. Not a percent — Settings.default_tax_rate is the percent form ('8.9'); divide it by 100 before sending. Values above 1 are rejected. Kept to six places, a percent to four (0.08875 means 8.875%); a finer rate is rounded half up.

CustomerResponse.title: CustomerResponse
CustomerResponse.description:
A customer as every customer endpoint answers it. Three balances,
each in home dollars, summed from the open documents (the stored
Customer.balance column is never written; services/contact_balances):

* ``balance`` is what the customer's own open documents leave: its
  invoices, net of the credit memos and unapplied payments it holds.
* ``billed_balance`` is what sits on the customer's A/R: its own
  balance plus that of the sub-customers billed with it, the figure
  its A/R Aging row shows and what a property owes for its tenants.
  The same as ``balance`` for a customer with no sub-customer billed
  with it (2.31.1 gate, W-61).
* ``rollup_balance`` is set on a parent only: its own balance plus
  every sub-customer's, billed with it or not, what the property has
  open altogether (its page's roll-up). None otherwise.

DepositDetailResponse.title: DepositDetailResponse
DepositDetailResponse.description:
One deposit with the payments it took, each in the shape Make
Deposits lists a waiting payment — what the bank register's link to a
deposit opens. A void deposit has given its payments back to the list,
so it names none.

DepositResponse.title: DepositResponse
DepositResponse.description:
A deposit made: its journal entry id, the bank account and amount,
how many payments it took (None for a deposit that named none — made
before deposits kept their list, imported, or posted by hand), and whether it is void or
on a reconciled bank statement.

DepositUpdate.title: DepositUpdate
DepositUpdate.description:
Edit a deposit in place from the register (#388): its date, slip
reference, class and job, and which undeposited payments it takes
(`line_ids` — the ones it holds now plus any still waiting). A field
left out keeps what the deposit has. A deposit on a reconciled bank
statement keeps its amount and date; only its reference, class and job
can change then.

DetailType.title: DetailType
DetailType.description:
QuickBooks' fifteen account types (#390). The detail type refines
`account_type` and may never contradict it: BASE_TYPE_OF is the pair.

DiscountTaken.title: DiscountTaken
DiscountTaken.description:
The early-payment discount already taken on a document (#664): the
amount and the number of the credit memo (invoice) or vendor credit
(bill) that is it. Shown in place of the offer once it is spent.

EnterRequest.title: EnterRequest
EnterRequest.description:
Enter now: the occurrence the page showed (its scheduled date), dated
that date unless a date is given. An occurrence that is no longer the
schedule's next one is refused (409) and nothing is posted; left out
(an API caller), the schedule's next date is entered.

Values above 1 are rejected. Kept to six places, a percent to four (0.08875 means 8.875%); a finer rate is rounded half up.

EstimateTotals.title: EstimateTotals
EstimateTotals.description:
The bid math (#551): the lines stay at cost, the four markups are their
own figures under the subtotal, the bid total is subtotal + markups
(pre-tax), and the package / alternate / unit-price breakdowns.

Values above 1 are rejected. Kept to six places, a percent to four (0.08875 means 8.875%); a finer rate is rounded half up.

ExpenseCreate.title: ExpenseCreate
ExpenseCreate.description:
One paid receipt: money already left a bank or credit-card account.
DR the expense account (or, with `lines`, each line's account for its
share), CR the account it was paid from. Send `lines` or the older
single `expense_account_id`, not both; the lines add up to `amount`
(left out, `amount` is their sum).

ExpenseLineIn.title: ExpenseLineIn
ExpenseLineIn.description:
One line of an expense (#599): the account it is recorded to, its
share of the amount paid, its own memo, and the class, job, cost code
and cost type it carries. Left out, class and job are the expense's.

FeedAddAll.title: FeedAddAll
FeedAddAll.description:
Add all categorised, with each row's own picks (#671). A line not
listed posts with its category alone, as before.

FeedExcludeAll.title: FeedExcludeAll
FeedExcludeAll.description: Exclude all shown (#705): the review list's statement line ids.

FeedLinePicks.title: FeedLinePicks
FeedLinePicks.description:
What the To review row chose for one line besides its category
(#671): the entry's class and job, and the vendor or customer it names.

InvitePayload.title: InvitePayload
InvitePayload.description:
Invite your accountant (#345): a sign-in with a one-time password,
the Accountant role unless another is asked for, and an end date if
the engagement has one.

tax_rate.description: Tax rate as a FRACTION of the taxable subtotal: 0.089 means 8.9%. Not a percent — Settings.default_tax_rate is the percent form ('8.9'); divide it by 100 before sending. Values above 1 are rejected. Kept to six places, a percent to four (0.08875 means 8.875%); a finer rate is rounded half up.

JobSummary.title: JobSummary
JobSummary.description: Profitability figures for one job (all-time unless dated).

JournalEntryUpdate.title: JournalEntryUpdate
JournalEntryUpdate.description:
The journal form's fields again, to rewrite a hand-entered entry in
place from the register (#388). An entry a completed reconciliation
holds keeps its amount and date; a change that moves an amount between
accounts in that period is refused with 409 until `confirm_reconciled`
is true.

LienWaiverCreate.title: LienWaiverCreate
LienWaiverCreate.description:
A waiver for one payment and job. The amount is the part of the payment
applied to that job's invoices; `job_id` may be left out when the payment
pays one job's invoices only, and must be given when it spans more than
one. The application comes from the job's invoice; the through date
defaults to the application's period (else the payment's date).

MemorizedLineIn.title: MemorizedLineIn
MemorizedLineIn.description:
One line of a memorized bill (an item or account, a quantity and
rate or an amount alone) or journal entry (an account and a debit or a
credit), with the memo, job, class, cost code, cost type, function and
billable mark either kind carries. Checked by the document's own line
schema for its kind, so the rules are Enter Bill's and the journal
form's.

anyOf.description: Tax rate as a FRACTION of the taxable subtotal: 0.089 means 8.9%. Not a percent — Settings.default_tax_rate is the percent form ('8.9'); divide it by 100 before sending. Values above 1 are rejected. Kept to six places, a percent to four (0.08875 means 8.875%); a finer rate is rounded half up.

MemorizedUpdate.title: MemorizedUpdate
MemorizedUpdate.description:
Whatever is sent changes, the rest stays; lines, when sent, replace
the lines. The kind is fixed. next_date moves the schedule (a skipped
month, a day changed); the day it names becomes the day of the month
the schedule holds to.

MovementType.title: MovementType
MovementType.description: Reason for an inventory movement row.

NachaOriginating.title: NachaOriginating
NachaOriginating.description:
What an ACH file's header says about the originator. Every field is
optional: what is not sent comes from Settings → Direct Deposit (ACH),
so a client that saved them there posts an empty body.

OcrAttachRequest.description:
POST /api/ocr/intake/{intake_id}/attach — link the scan to a document.

A sales receipt is stored as an invoice (is_sales_receipt=true), so the
frontend sends entity_type="invoice" for both sales receipts and regular
invoices; "bill" covers the Enter Bill form.

OcrField.title: OcrField
OcrField.description: An extracted value plus how much the parser trusts it.

OcrReceiptResponse.title: OcrReceiptResponse
OcrReceiptResponse.description:
POST /api/ocr/receipt — extraction result for a scanned receipt.

When `ocr_available` is False the scan could not run (Tesseract missing)
and `message` explains how to enable it; the other fields stay default.
`intake_id` references the stored scan so the frontend can attach it to
the document after save (POST /api/ocr/intake/{id}/attach).

OcrRegionRequest.title: OcrRegionRequest
OcrRegionRequest.description:
POST /api/ocr/intake/{intake_id}/region — OCR one typed rectangle of
a stored scan (the v2 box-to-fix canvas). Pixel coordinates in the
intake image's space (the same space /intake/{id}/image serves).

OcrStatusResponse.title: OcrStatusResponse
OcrStatusResponse.description: GET /api/ocr/status — is an OCR engine usable, and which one?

OcrWordBox.title: OcrWordBox
OcrWordBox.description:
A recognized word (or line, engine-dependent) with pixel bounds —
the v2 box-to-fix canvas draws these over the scanned image.

OpeningQuarterInput.title: OpeningQuarterInput
OpeningQuarterInput.description:
What the old system paid in one calendar quarter (1-4), as its
payroll reports show it: the 941 for the quarter carries these.

OpeningStateInput.title: OpeningStateInput
OpeningStateInput.description:
One state's figures for one quarter. SUTA is a state's own: its
wage base fills from its own wages.

POConvertToBill.title: POConvertToBill
POConvertToBill.description:
The To Bill dialog's choices: an account for each line that needs one,
and optionally the amount to bill this period (partial billing, #553).
Lines left out post to their item's expense account, else the vendor's
default, and bill their full remaining.

Values above 1 are rejected. Kept to six places, a percent to four (0.08875 means 8.875%); a finer rate is rounded half up.

PayApplicationCreate.title: PayApplicationCreate
PayApplicationCreate.description:
A new owner pay application. Its lines are pre-filled from the job's
schedule of values, so only the header is sent.

PayApplicationUpdate.title: PayApplicationUpdate
PayApplicationUpdate.description:
Edit a draft/submitted application: this period and stored per line,
plus the header figures.

PaymentApply.title: PaymentApply
PaymentApply.description:
Apply the unapplied part of an earlier payment to open invoices of
the same customer.

PaymentDiscountAdd.title: PaymentDiscountAdd
PaymentDiscountAdd.description:
An early-payment discount taken after the payment that paid the rest
(#665): the customer paid 98 of 100 within the window, and the 2 is
recorded against that payment, dated as it is.

PaymentDiscountResponse.title: PaymentDiscountResponse
PaymentDiscountResponse.description:
A discount the customer took with this payment: the credit memo
applied to the invoice (#664).

PaymentTermUpdate.title: PaymentTermUpdate
PaymentTermUpdate.description:
Whatever is sent changes; the rule as a whole is checked again. A
rule field sent as null clears it (the discount, say).

PayoutRequest.title: PayoutRequest
PayoutRequest.description:
A provider payout that arrived without a bank feed (#584): the net
that landed in the bank, the processor's fee for the batch (0 when it
was already booked at capture), the date, and the bank account.

PayrollOpeningInput.title: PayrollOpeningInput
PayrollOpeningInput.description:
An employee's opening balance for a year: the old system's figures
quarter by quarter through `as_of`, the day before the first SlowBooks
pay run. Benefit amounts are for the year. Once a run in the year is
processed for the employee a change needs `reason` (it is a
correction, and the audit trail keeps it).

ReconciliationCreate.title: ReconciliationCreate
ReconciliationCreate.description:
`account_id` is the ledger account; `bank_account_id` (a feed) is
accepted for older callers.

ReconciliationUpdate.title: ReconciliationUpdate
ReconciliationUpdate.description:
Correct the statement's date or ending balance while the
reconciliation is in progress (#389): a transposed digit was a fresh
start. Both optional; an omitted field is left as it was.

RetypedSubAccount.title: RetypedSubAccount
RetypedSubAccount.description:
A sub-account the PUT's cascade retyped (#416): named so an API client
knows which ones changed with the parent.

SalesReceiptCreate.title: SalesReceiptCreate
SalesReceiptCreate.description:
One-screen sales receipt: an invoice and its full payment entered
together (QB's "Enter Sales Receipts"). No terms/due date — payment is
at the time of sale.

ScheduleRow.title: ScheduleRow
ScheduleRow.description:
One line of the Memorized transactions page: a recurring invoice
(kind "invoice", its id under /api/recurring), a memorized bill or a
memorized journal entry (its id under /api/memorized).

SetupPayload.title: SetupPayload
SetupPayload.description:
First-run setup. Password is required; everything else is optional and
falls back to the DEFAULT_SETTINGS values if blank.

StatementCategory.title: StatementCategory
StatementCategory.description:
The category picked for a statement line in the review list (null
clears it). Kept on the line, so Add all posts it and a reload shows
it.

StatementPayout.title: StatementPayout
StatementPayout.description:
Record an unmatched deposit as a provider payout (#584): the server
builds the split (CR clearing the gross, DR the fee, DR bank the net)
so the clearing and fee account ids stay off the client. `gross` is the
amount cleared from the clearing account; the fee is gross − the
statement net, which must not be negative.

StatementVendors.title: StatementVendors
StatementVendors.description:
Added feed lines whose payee should become (or be linked to) a
vendor (#491).

TermsDatesResponse.title: TermsDatesResponse
TermsDatesResponse.description:
What a date and terms make of a document: the forms show it as the
person picks, so the page never computes a due date of its own.

TransferCreate.title: TransferCreate
TransferCreate.description:
Money between two bank/card accounts. Paying a card is a transfer
from the bank to the card.

VendorCompliance.title: VendorCompliance
VendorCompliance.description:
What a Sub vendor's paperwork looks like at pay time (#553). A missing
W-9 or COI only warns; an expired COI blocks payment unless overridden.

Values above 1 are rejected. Kept to six places, a percent to four (0.08875 means 8.875%); a finer rate is rounded half up.

ZeroTotalConfirmation.title: ZeroTotalConfirmation
ZeroTotalConfirmation.description:
The optional body of Duplicate and of an estimate's Convert: a copy
that adds up to $0.00 is made only with ``allow_zero_total: true``, and
one that takes the payer past their credit limit only with
``allow_over_credit_limit: true`` (#256; Duplicate since the 2.31.1
gate, W-79).

app__schemas__banking__BankAccountCreate.title: BankAccountCreate
app__schemas__banking__BankAccountCreate.description:
A bank feed / statement identity for a ledger account that has
bank_kind set. An opening balance posts a journal entry against 3900
Opening Balance Equity; it is what the statement says (cash in the
bank, or the amount owed on a card). When the ledger already carries
the account on the opening date, only a difference can post, and only
with `post_difference` set (the user confirmed it).

BearerToken.description: Scoped API token from Settings -> API Tokens, sent as `Authorization: Bearer sbp_...`. Session cookies from POST /api/auth/login are accepted equivalently.
